overview: The two types of photoreceptor cells in the retina, specialised for different lighting conditions and types of vision.
genZNote: Rods: your night-vision crew, no colour, just brightness. Cones: your daylight colour squad.

aspects.label: Main Function
aspects.valueA: Detect light intensity, enabling vision in dim light (scotopic vision); cannot detect colour.
aspects.valueB: Detect colour and fine detail in bright light (photopic vision).

aspects.label: Relative Number in Retina
aspects.valueA: Much more numerous (~120 million per eye).
aspects.valueB: Fewer in number (~6 million per eye).

aspects.label: Photopigment
aspects.valueB: Contains iodopsin, with three types tuned to red, green, and blue light.

aspects.label: Distribution in Retina
aspects.valueB: Concentrated in the fovea centralis, the point of sharpest vision.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: The fovea centralis, packed almost entirely with cones, is why your sharpest, most colourful vision is exactly where you're directly looking.
overlay.memoryTrick: Rods = night vision, no colour (rods 'run' in the dark). Cones = colour, daylight.
overlay.commonMisconception: Colour blindness is not caused by a problem with rods — it results specifically from a deficiency or absence of one or more types of cones.
